{"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["app/tickets.py:11:config-class"], "search": "from pydantic import BaseModel", "replace": "from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict", "explanation": "ConfigDict is needed for the v2 model_config assignment. Per the migration guide (Changes to config), v2 configuration is set via a model_config dict/ConfigDict rather than a nested Config class."}, {"finding_ids": ["app/tickets.py:11:config-class"], "search": "    class Config:
        anystr_strip_whitespace = True", "replace": "    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)", "explanation": "The nested `class Config` is deprecated in v2. Per the migration guide, use `model_config = ConfigDict(...)`, and the renamed setting `anystr_strip_whitespace` becomes `str_strip_whitespace`. Behavior is unchanged: string fields are still stripped of surrounding whitespace."}], "notes": "The config-class finding is addressed by the two edits above: the nested Config is replaced with model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True), and the ConfigDict import is added.

Not changed, but please review: from_db_rows passes integer primary keys from the database driver into `ticket_id: str`. Pydantic v1 coerced int to str by default. Pydantic v2 does not coerce int to str by default, so Ticket(ticket_id=1, ...) will now raise a ValidationError at runtime. This is a behavioral change outside the config finding, so I left it alone. Possible fixes are to convert with str(r[0]) in from_db_rows, or to set coerce_numbers_to_str=True in the ConfigDict (the latter also affects float and Decimal fields, though this model has none). The right choice depends on whether the caller should own the conversion.

No other v1 APIs appear in this file, so no other edits were needed. The List import is still used and was left unchanged."}
